headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via AutoGPT’s filesystem/CLI surfaces; LlamaFactory is read-only and offline, limiting pairwise blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and access the filesystem, while LlamaFactory exposes no input channels or write surfaces. The pairwise pathway is indirect, but if AutoGPT ingests LlamaFactory-generated files or prompts from a shared workspace, instruction-like content could be treated as trusted. Uncertainty about the shared workspace escalates from low to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF AutoGPT reads LlamaFactory-produced text as instructions
mitigations: Disable AutoGPT file ingestion for untrusted outputs
Add a prompt-injection filter on imported text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and make allowlisted network calls, but LlamaFactory has no filesystem read/write, clipboard, or network egress. No sensitive data class is declared for either agent, so the main leakage path is limited to accidental exposure through a shared workspace if one is introduced. The pairwise risk stays low because B cannot actively exfiltrate.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is mounted between the agents
IF sensitive files are placed in AutoGPT’s workspace
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared directories

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, but LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, or use subprocesses. There is no overlapping write authority, so direct capability conflict is minimal. The only plausible conflict is if an operator manually gives both agents the same mutable directory, which is not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are granted the same writable repository
IF an operator asks both to edit the same files concurrently

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs that another system may consume, and LlamaFactory can produce model artifacts or text, but B has no built-in verification or action-taking authority shown. If AutoGPT’s output is fed into LlamaFactory workflows without review, errors can propagate across work products. Because the interaction is inferred rather than documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is used as input to LlamaFactory workflows
IF no human review occurs between generation and reuse

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile declares regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies. AutoGPT and LlamaFactory are both open-source and the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or other compliance-sensitive flows. With no declared compliance mismatch, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced into either agent
IF residency or retention requirements are imposed externally
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair
